title: Derived categories with allowable torsion
statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ be a set of primes and let $T$ be a scheme. Using the derived categories and cohomology sheaves of abelian etale sheaves from [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], write

$$
D^b_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et}),\qquad
D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et})
$$

for the full triangulated subcategories of $D^b(T_{\Et})$ and $D^+(T_{\Et})$, respectively, consisting of objects $K$ such that every geometric stalk of every cohomology sheaf $H^q(K)$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is a torsion group whose prime divisors belong to $\mathcal P$. Explicitly, for every integer $q$, every geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, and every $x\in H^q(K)_{\bar t}$, there exists a positive integer $n$ with $n x=0$ and with all prime divisors of $n$ in $\mathcal P$. The inherited triangulated structures are supplied by [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory], applied to the allowable-torsion sheaves using the exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact].

proof.text: For each geometric point use its sheafFiber functor. Finite-limit preservation follows from the AB5 instance for abelian groups, shrunk to the site universe; the skyscraper adjunction supplies finite-colimit preservation. Thus stalks take monomorphisms to injections, epimorphisms to surjections, and short exact sequences to short exact sequences. An allowable annihilator transports along an injection or a surjection, proving closure of allowableTorsionSheafProperty under subobjects and quotients.

The stalk of a zero sheaf is a zero abelian group. Its unique element is killed by 1, whose set of prime divisors is empty. Thus allowableTorsionSheafProperty contains zero, including when P is empty.

For a short exact sequence A -> E -> C of sheaves and an element x of a geometric stalk of E, choose a positive allowable n annihilating its image in C. Exactness gives an element y of the stalk of A whose image is n times x. Choose a positive allowable m annihilating y. Then mn annihilates x. It is positive, and each prime divisor of mn divides m or n, hence belongs to P. This proves closure under extensions. Subobject closure also gives invariance under isomorphisms. The argument uses no assumption that all members of P are prime.

Apply the already-proved source-library theorem DerivedCategory.homologyProperty_isTriangulated, attached among the declarations of prop-constructible-derived-subcategory, to the closure instances just proved. The required kernel and cokernel closure follow from subobject and quotient closure. The homology property is invariant under isomorphisms. Intersect it with the standard t-structure plus or bounded object property, whose triangulated and isomorphism-closure instances are already available in the derived-category interface. Instance inference supplies the four named theorems. This uses the generic source theorem directly, without the duplicate statement-only cohomology_in_weak_serre_subcategory wrapper.

split_report.summary: Definition split using the existing derived-category and geometric-stalk definitions. The allowable-prime condition is written explicitly in the item, so no additional clause-restating node is necessary. The abelian coefficient case is the blueprint definition; source module-sheaf predicates were read as corroborating definitions, not as completed proofs of this complete definition. Maintainer repair: record the actual logged Mathlib searches and cite the generic cohomology-in-weak-Serre-class theorem and the existing exactness-of-stalks leaf for the claimed triangulated structures.
split_report.blueprint: The sole definition clause of the blueprint is realized: bounded and bounded-below full subcategories with the positive-annihilator allowable-prime condition on every cohomology stalk. Whole-blueprint search for torsion, geometric stalks, and derived categories found no other node defining both these subcategories.
split_report.well_definedness: Let B be the full class of abelian etale sheaves satisfying the displayed stalk condition. It contains zero (annihilator 1) and is invariant under isomorphism. Subgroups and quotients of allowable-torsion groups inherit positive allowable annihilators. For 0 -> A -> E -> C -> 0 and e in E, kill its image in C by an allowable n; then n e comes from A and is killed by an allowable m, so mn kills e and has only allowable prime factors. Thus the group class is closed under extensions. Exactness of geometric stalks (prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact) makes B closed under kernels, cokernels, and extensions. The cited generic lemma supplies the triangulated structure on all complexes with cohomology in B and on its bounded and bounded-below intersections. These are precisely the two full subcategories defined in the item.
